The game's good fun, but has some issues that should hopefully be ironed out during early access.  

Biggest issue is balance.  Early game especially if you get a shotgun crab or a launcher crab (or some other form of armed crab in general) you might as well restart because even if you can avoid all of it's insane attacks, it's health is so high you'll be wailing on it exclusively for 30s+ unless you got some lucky items.  Also all of the skull enemies are horrible, but the fire skulls are the worst as they're basically unavoidable damage, especially early on.

While there've been very few bugs in general, the few I've found are usually soft-locking a run.  E.g., enemies getting stuck under the map where they sometimes can shoot you but you can't shoot back.  There's no isaac style door opening system after x minutes either, as far as I can tell, meaning you're wiped in this case.  Obviously this is an early access issue but still.

After you unlock all the guns you can use keys to get a random item for your next run.  The way this was implemented isn't great and I hope it gets iterated on.  

Again, the game is really fun but it's in early access, expect hiccups and hope the devs continue support / improvements.

AS OF WRITING THIS GAME IS IN EARLY ACCESS
{NOTE: I am just  random gamer. I have no industry experience or programming knowledge, thus have no real idea of how anything would actually be fixed so take my suggestions with a grain of salt}

There is a gem of a rougelike shooter here. It is distinctly early access and needing content/polish, but the solid concepts and core gameplay present combined with the robust developer roadmap and already consistent updates make me very very hopeful for this games future.

At the moment I enjoy it, and quite a lot, but the lack of variety and content in a few areas make it difficult for me to play for more than around an hour at a time. 

Thoughts:
-Spiked chests never feel worth it and I have picked them once. 
-Some modifiers are pretty unreasonable to deal with (elemental explosions and shrapnel come to mind)
-Armor isn't common enough for it to feel worth it. (Suggestion: Maybe have armor be it's own chest type? Having an option that would be dedicated to armor seems like a way to make it viable. Maybe even replace spiked chests?)
-Music is fun but after a while gets a bit repetitive. Then again it's also not necessarily my preferred type of music so this is a very subjective point.

I would LOVE to see more parkour levels, the movement in this game is very fun and interesting as well as being polished. (Maybe even a dedicated parkour mode with a bunch of levels?)
I also have my fingers crossed for a pvp multiplayer, as I feel this game would be suited well for it. (That said multiplayer is a little jank, which doesn't affect the gameplay due to it being PvE.)

Some less specific things that I feel could use some work/fine tuning:
-some button interactions are unresponsive
-enemy movements/attacks/patterns are difficult to discern
-enemies can often feel either too spongy or too fragile
-melee range (of players and enemies alike) are not clear
-weapon unlock/progression is not very balanced for single player

I wholeheartedly recommend this game. There's a need for content, but I am confident it will be filled. Excited to be here for the development.

A very fun twitch shooter - like Quake, Tribes, Reflex. 4 player co-op. 
Roguelite(?) mechanics so each run will be different even if you don't change your loadout. 
Movement feels good, responsive. Just holding shift to slide and jumping feels like skating, the double jump is responsive but carries momentum with it.
The gunplay is largely satisfying so far. There's bullet trajectory modifiers so you can get some very fun effects going on.
The runs have save & quit anytime.

Game is fun, and the fighting and movement feels pretty good.

But most importantly, the game seems like a true passion project, with cosmetics that are unlocked through gameplay rather than microtransactions. I'd claim that the game is worth it's cost already, and I truly believe that it will only get better over time.
